title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 121
paragraphs: Having spoken thus, Astyages sent Cyrus away. When he arrived at the house of Cambyses, his parents received him, and afterwards, when they learned who he was, they welcomed him with great joy, for they had supposed without doubt that their son had perished straightway after his birth. They asked how he had survived. He told them, saying that before this he had not known but had been utterly mistaken; on the way, however, he had learned all his own fortunes. For he had supposed without doubt that he was the son of the herdsman of Astyages, but since his journey from the city began he had learned the whole story from those who were conducting him. And he said that he had been brought up by the wife of the herdsman, and he continued to praise her throughout, so that Kyno was the chief figure in his tale. And his parents took up this name from him, and in order that their son might be thought by the Persians to have been preserved in a more supernatural manner, they set on foot a report that Cyrus, when he was exposed, had been reared by a bitch (“kyno” in Greek means bitch). And from this source has come that report.
